chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Ghaleb, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatarri, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Ishaq ibn Jarir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The month is thus, thus, and thus,' joining his palms and spreading them. Then he said, 'And thus, thus, and thus,' then closing one finger in the final spread of his hands, which is the thumb.' I said, 'Is the month of Ramadan always complete, or is it a month among the months?' He said, 'It is a month among the months.' Then he said, 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) fasted among you for twenty-nine days, so they came to him and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, we have seen the crescent.' He said, 'Break your fast.'
ai.seo_question: Is the month of Ramadan always 30 days or can it be 29 days according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the lunar nature of Ramadan by citing the Prophet’s hand gestures and Imam Ali’s practice of fasting twenty-nine days, establishing that the month is variable rather than fixed. It underscores the Shia scholarly principle that actual moon sighting (*ru'yah*) takes precedence over mathematical calculation (*hisab*) for determining the end of the month, as evidenced by the command to break the fast upon sighting. This reinforces the flexibility of the Islamic calendar and the authority of the Imams in interpreting prophetic traditions regarding timekeeping.
